anchor.quote: simple-rest: pass meta.signal to the axios call in getList, getMany, getOne and custom (GET).

behaviours: getList passes meta.signal as the `signal` option in the axios request config, together with the existing `headers` option.
getMany passes meta.signal as the `signal` option in the axios request config.
getOne passes meta.signal as the `signal` option in the axios request config.
custom with a GET (default) method passes meta.signal as the `signal` option in the axios request config.

When the AbortController linked to meta.signal is aborted while a getList, getMany, getOne or custom GET request is in flight, the returned promise rejects and the HTTP request is cancelled (proved by a test with an AbortController).
When meta.signal is already aborted before the call, getList, getMany, getOne and custom GET reject without the request finishing.

When meta is undefined or meta has no `signal`, the axios config has no `signal` key. For example, getList with pagination mode 'off' and no filters still calls httpClient.get(url, { headers: undefined }) exactly as before, and the existing simple-rest tests pass with unchanged expectations.
The meta.headers and meta.method handling in getList, getMany and getOne is unchanged.
create, update and deleteOne do not read meta.signal and send the same request config as before.
custom with method post, put, patch or delete sends the same request config as before.
The exported `dataProvider(apiUrl, httpClient)` signature and the `axiosInstance` export are unchanged.
documentation/docs/data/packages/simple-rest/index.md says that getList, getMany, getOne and custom (GET) forward meta.signal to axios, so that requests are cancelled when the query is cancelled.
A changeset file in .changeset/ declares a `minor` bump for "@refinedev/simple-rest" and describes meta.signal forwarding.

anchor.quote: rest: forward meta.signal to its HTTP client for read methods.

behaviours: getList passes params.meta.signal as the ky `signal` option.
getOne passes params.meta.signal as the ky `signal` option.
getMany (when configured in options) passes params.meta.signal as the ky `signal` option.
custom with method GET passes params.meta.signal as the ky `signal` option.

When the AbortController linked to meta.signal is aborted while a getList, getOne, getMany or custom GET request is in flight, the returned promise rejects and the request is cancelled (proved by a test with an AbortController against a delayed nock response).

When meta is undefined or meta has no `signal`, the read methods send the same request as before (same endpoint, headers and searchParams), and the existing packages/rest tests pass with unchanged expectations.
create, createMany, update, updateMany, deleteOne and deleteMany do not read meta.signal and behave as before.
The built-in options in packages/rest/src/data-providers (simple-rest, nestjsx-crud, strapi-v4) inherit signal forwarding through createDataProvider, with no change to their option files.
The exported `createDataProvider(apiURL, baseOptions, kyOptions)` signature and its `{ kyInstance, dataProvider }` return shape are unchanged.
documentation/docs/data/packages/rest-data-provider/index.md says that the read methods forward meta.signal to ky, so that requests are cancelled when the query is cancelled.
A changeset file in .changeset/ declares a `minor` bump for "@refinedev/rest" and describes meta.signal forwarding.
modules.name: rest signal forwarding

questions.affects: Which requests in @refinedev/rest (packages/rest/src/create-data-provider.ts) can be cancelled, and how far the rest module's scope and tests reach.
questions.if_wrong: If custom GET is left out, useCustom requests in rest keep running after unmount, unlike simple-rest. If the signal is added to custom mutations (post/put/patch/delete), a write could be aborted halfway, and the server may apply the change while the client sees a failure.
questions.q: Which @refinedev/rest methods count as 'read methods': getList, getOne and getMany only, or also custom when its method is GET? Also, should custom forward the signal for every HTTP method, or only for GET?

questions.affects: Whether users see an 'Error (status code: undefined)' toast when a request is cancelled, and whether files outside the two provider modules (core hooks or the simple-rest axios interceptor) are in scope.
questions.if_wrong: If we rely only on TanStack's behaviour and some path (for example a manual queryClient.cancelQueries without revert, or a signal aborted by user code) still surfaces the error, users get false error toasts. If we add a core guard when one is not wanted, we break the 'No core changes expected' scope and change notification behaviour for every data provider.
questions.q: For 'Aborted requests don't show error notifications': is it enough to rely on TanStack Query reverting a cancelled query (so useList/useOne never reach isError), or must a provider-level or core-level guard also stop notifications when an abort error (axios CanceledError / ERR_CANCELED, ky AbortError) reaches the hooks? Note that the ticket says 'No core changes expected', and the simple-rest axios interceptor (packages/simple-rest/src/utils/axios.ts) turns every error, including cancellations, into an HttpError with an undefined message and statusCode.

questions.affects: Which test files the units must write, and whether core test files (packages/core) come into scope even though no core source changes.
questions.if_wrong: If provider-level tests are accepted but the team expected hook-level proof, AC-1 could be judged unmet. If hook-level tests are required but not planned, the build unit has no core test file in its SCOPE and cannot satisfy the criterion.
questions.q: Must 'Changing filters or unmounting aborts the in-flight request' be proved by an integration test that drives useList/useOne through @refinedev/core (changing filters, unmounting), or are provider-level tests enough, where a test passes a signal from its own AbortController and aborts it?

questions.affects: Which documentation files are in the modules' SCOPE, and where users learn that cancellation is supported.
questions.if_wrong: If the wrong page is updated, the docs acceptance criterion is judged unmet, or authors of custom data providers never learn they should read meta.signal.
questions.q: Which pages are 'Data provider docs': the package pages (documentation/docs/data/packages/simple-rest/index.md and documentation/docs/data/packages/rest-data-provider/index.md), the general data provider page (documentation/docs/data/data-provider/index.md, which does not mention signal today), the package READMEs, or all of them?

sealed_acceptance_criteria.text: Changing filters or unmounting aborts the in-flight request (verified by tests with an AbortController).
Aborted requests don't show error notifications.
Behaviour is unchanged when no signal is present.
Data provider docs mention meta.signal support.
